A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rank-Surprisal Ratio study. The text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original teacher–student distillation experiments, simulations, correlation analyses, ablations and selection experiments, including GPQA evaluation in Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds runtime measurements, a No Selection comparison, further metric ablations and trajectory analyses.

M1.justification: The trajectory-level RSR formula, rank clipping and training/selection procedures are retained. V4 explicitly specifies dataset-level weighting in A.8 and an equivalent top-k implementation in Appendix C. These expand the documentation without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Section 7 newly reports preliminary cross-problem subset-selection experiments on unspecified internal data, extending the reported selection scenario. The NuminaMath training problems, four mathematical benchmarks and GPQA-Diamond are retained. Non-CoT evaluation remains future work, and the internal-data coverage is not detailed.

E2.justification: V4 adds a No Selection baseline to the trajectory-selection comparison in Table 15 and entropy, weighted-sum and product alternatives in Table 14. Existing comparators remain. G-Norm, Influence Score and LLM-judged Quality also participate in the new runtime comparison.

E3.justification: The added No Selection experiment combines one 5,000-trajectory dataset per teacher into 55,000 training samples, introducing a data-volume comparison with 5,000 selected samples. Appendix C adds a timing protocol using 5,000 DeepSeek-R1 trajectories and LLaMA-3.1-8B. Existing benchmark protocols, model configurations and training hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands diagnostic analysis: it tests five additional metric variants, compares selection with a larger unfiltered training set, benchmarks computational cost, examines selected trajectories' length and correctness, and adds token-level case studies. These address aggregation, alternative formulations, efficiency and selection behavior beyond the analyses already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report three generation runs per teacher, three fine-tuning seeds for trajectory selection, and four evaluations per problem. Correlation reporting practices are retained. V4 adds descriptive dataset statistics but no confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or changed uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Matched primary results, including Tables 1–7 and GPQA results, are unchanged, but substantial supplementary findings are added. Table 15 reports average accuracy of 52.5 for No Selection with 55k samples versus 51.3 for RSR with 5k. Table 14 adds simple-aggregation correlation of 0.838 versus RSR's 0.856. Table 10 reports 1, 6, 32 and 12 GPU-hours for RSR, G-Norm, Influence Score and LLM-judged Quality, respectively. Additional trajectory statistics and token measurements are also reported.

T1.justification: V4 A.8 adds a formal dataset-level RSR definition and derives its equivalence to a ratio of summed trajectory-average ranks and surprisals. Appendix C adds an O(TV) complexity argument. The original trajectory-level equations and simulation assumptions remain unchanged; no new theorem or substantive proof framework appears.

C1.justification: The central informative-alignment claim, average Spearman correlation of 0.86, and trajectory/teacher-selection contributions are retained. V4 expands the introduction's contribution statement to include broader applicability to non-CoT data and subset selection, presented mainly as exploratory discussion.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands mechanism and applicability discussions. Appendix D attributes teacher differences to phrasing, reasoning pace and analytical depth, and interprets selection statistics as evidence beyond length or correctness. E.3.1 proposes why LLaMA benefits more from additional data. Section 7 discusses cross-problem confounding, while Limitations more explicitly distinguishes GPQA transfer from selection on newly generated non-mathematical trajectories.

D1.justification: V1 provides code access; v4 additionally reports releasing all 33 generated datasets and student-specific RSR-selected datasets, with explicit dataset access information. It documents dataset-level aggregation, FlashAttention-2 and top-k rank computation. The illustrative SFT cost changes from six hours for a 14B model to seven hours for a 7B model on eight H200 GPUs; this is not a same-model timing comparison.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations to FlashAttention-2, Self-distillation Enables Continual Learning, STaR, and Vygotsky and Cole's Mind in Society. It connects motivation to the zone of proximal development and expands related-work coverage of self-distillation. The original research positioning and cited comparison methods are largely retained.

P1.justification: V4 edits wording, clarifies terminology and adds cross-references while retaining the main narrative. It inserts a Broader Applicability section and reorganizes appendix material into separate computational-cost, diagnostic-analysis, additional-results and complete-table sections. Most existing explanations remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V4 adds runtime and trajectory-statistics tables and an extensive color-coded token visualization in Tables 10–12. It expands ablation and selection tables, adds a length column and clipped-rank/performance rows, and reorganizes appendix displays. The three existing figures are retained with limited presentation refinements.

improvement.justification: V4 improves reproducibility through explicit aggregation definitions and reported data releases. New cost, No Selection and ablation comparisons make practical utility easier to assess, including the substantial benefit of more data for LLaMA. These are useful gains over v1's already extensive empirical study. The improvement remains limited because the new mechanism explanations are largely illustrative and the internal subset-selection evidence is only briefly described.
